references.text: God gave Moses the command to consecrate the people and have them wash their clothes as preparation for the Lord's coming on the mountain.
The requirement of holiness for God's people is repeated, where the Lord commands Israel to consecrate themselves because He is holy.
Washing of clothes as part of cleansing rituals to become ceremonially clean before God.
The Levites had to wash their clothes as part of the purification before they could serve the Lord.
The people were asked to consecrate themselves in preparation for the Lord's action among them.
Joshua commanded the people to consecrate themselves before the Lord would do miraculous things among them.
Joshua told the people to consecrate themselves in preparation for the Lord's presence and action.
The New Testament speaks of approaching God with a pure heart and body washed with clean water, as a parallel to Old Testament cleansing.
Those who have washed their robes white in the Lamb's blood, as fulfillment of the cleansing motif.
Both verses illustrate the theological principle of ritual washing as a necessary preparation for meeting God or performing holy service.
